items.q: Where does Squibb say the why lives, and what is DreamBrew's?
items.a: In **pain**. DreamBrew supports dreams; some profit should go back to buyers. His wound: left school at 15, and 25–30 years later the system still teaches **jobs, not dreams**. If the why is fuzzy, walk the other steps and come back.

items.q: What language shift births the brand, and how do you name it?
items.a: Drop **'one day I'll be.'** Say **'I am a coffee company.'** Name the baby. **Descriptive** (Dream Brew = product + mission) vs **invented** (Google: easier trademark/URLs, harder to explain). Then trademark + same handle everywhere — he bought 'Simon Squibb' back from a squatter.

items.q: How many samples do you need before you are allowed to start?
items.a: **One.** Not 10,000, not a million dollars. Book = one page a day. Clothing = one shop tee with your bits on it. AI mock or beg a supplier. One object is enough to get feedback and to show an investor it is real.

items.q: Who is the partner, and what split does he want?
items.a: Spouse who keeps the job, or a co-founder. **Opposite love/hate list, same why** (he loves camera; his wife hates it). **50% of something you love that works** beats **100% of nothing**. Self-made is a school-exam lie. 1+1=11.

items.q: How do you sit with an investor, and what if you skip them?
items.a: **Ask for advice, get money. Ask for money, get advice.** Act like you do not need the cheque. Cut burn so you are not begging — weakness = extra equity taken. Patience path: one tee → two → four (Gymshark / Ben Francis). Raise only if you really need it; cash then makes a day-to-day co-founder easier.

items.q: How do you test, then what actually launches the business?
items.a: Show **~10 possible customers** the sample, or a free waitlist page. HelpBnk: **12,000 signups in 2 days**. Jobs/keyboard is the exception; 9/10 you are not Jobs. Then **tell everyone**, including the other dog walker. He failed businesses only because he **stopped** — comic book lost $1M when it was not his why.
